spatial-u4969c3867218c16361-1.text: The main directions of spatial development of the Russian Federation define specific tasks aimed at overcoming spatial development challenges and problems and realizing opportunities, taking account of the principles of spatial development of the Russian Federation.
spatial-u4969c3867218c16361-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-ud7d1088dca631e6740-1.text: The main directions and tasks of spatial development of the Russian Federation include:
spatial-ud7d1088dca631e6740-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-udc822d77f627117ecc-1.text: creating a balanced territorial organization of the economy that promotes a supply-side economy aimed at increasing production of goods and services for the domestic market and the value added generated in the domestic economy, including by unlocking territories’ potential and creating conditions for accelerated industrial, scientific and technological cooperation among constituent entities of the Russian Federation, including through:
spatial-udc822d77f627117ecc-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-ua1d0d38f8c5369f81c-1.text: ensuring advance development of infrastructure, including transport and energy infrastructure, in anchor settlements where new investment projects with a substantial impact on the territory’s economy are being implemented;
spatial-ua1d0d38f8c5369f81c-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u504e210da409d09ccf-1.text: unlocking the economic potential of urban agglomerations and ensuring their scientific, technological and innovative development, including through the development of necessary transport, energy and social infrastructure;
spatial-u504e210da409d09ccf-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u5e54561a9b5bbfff08-1.text: increasing the depth of processing of mineral raw materials and timber; ensuring priority support in urban agglomerations, administrative centers of constituent entities of the Russian Federation and science cities for projects in high-technology and knowledge-intensive goods and services industries and in creative industries;
spatial-u5e54561a9b5bbfff08-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-uabdf118f63d0b1d765-1.text: supporting joint projects by industrial cluster participants to organize production of new types of raw materials, materials and components in order to strengthen production cooperation, and developing flexible cluster policy instruments, including a multilevel system of industrial clusters with differentiated support measures, including budget support, and an adaptive system of cross-sectoral and interregional cooperation responsive to changing conditions;
spatial-uabdf118f63d0b1d765-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u8aca0f89c3bf272c4b-1.text: creating conditions to accelerate modernization and development of industrial facilities in constituent entities of the Russian Federation, establishing sites with ready industrial and/or technological infrastructure and attracting new production facilities to such sites;
spatial-u8aca0f89c3bf272c4b-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u45d9db98ab6785eaf1-1.text: providing personnel for investment projects and other measures consistent with the priority development directions of the federal districts of the Russian Federation and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation;
spatial-u45d9db98ab6785eaf1-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-ua13847a0ef197b955f-1.text: expanding opportunities for venture financing of innovative and/or technological projects, primarily those implemented in Siberia, the Far East, urban agglomerations and science cities;
spatial-ua13847a0ef197b955f-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-uf89a3c7c5e7163689b-1.text: ensuring the full realization of export and cooperation potential in accordance with the Russian Federation’s foreign economic activity priorities, including through:
spatial-uf89a3c7c5e7163689b-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-udf49b9e7832e5db8cd-1.text: expanding the export offerings of Russian producers as export potential develops, competitiveness grows and new export specializations emerge in accordance with the Russian Federation’s foreign economic activity priorities, and improving the effectiveness of export potential;
spatial-udf49b9e7832e5db8cd-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u8afcbe3fadaee2c9ad-1.text: taking advantage of global energy transition trends by addressing developed countries’ demand for products with a low carbon footprint and developing countries’ need for access to technologies with low greenhouse gas emissions;
spatial-u8afcbe3fadaee2c9ad-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-uf896b4f95057d719c2-1.text: using instruments to support and promote exports to the markets of countries willing to engage constructively with the Russian Federation;
spatial-uf896b4f95057d719c2-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u06c4cca7f75a14c5d4-1.text: changing foreign trade regulation with regard to customs rules, the predictability of restrictions and the application of protective measures;
spatial-u06c4cca7f75a14c5d4-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u692244b991f0b1b670-1.text: developing cooperation between border regions and municipalities and bordering states, including the Republic of Azerbaijan, the Republic of Belarus, the Republic of Kazakhstan, the People’s Republic of China, the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea, Mongolia, the Republic of Abkhazia and the Republic of South Ossetia, and accelerating integration within the Eurasian Economic Union to create a single market for goods, works, services, capital and labor, including taking account of the spatial and infrastructure development plans of bordering states;
spatial-u692244b991f0b1b670-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u9bfa4070160a04423e-1.text: creating conditions for population and birth-rate growth in all constituent entities of the Russian Federation, primarily in territories where natural population decrease significantly exceeds the Russian average, including regions of the Central, Northwestern and Volga Federal Districts, through:
spatial-u9bfa4070160a04423e-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u5402b10fbd4c638946-1.text: ensuring priority support for enterprises implementing their own employee-family support programs, including the creation of jobs for parents of large families;
spatial-u5402b10fbd4c638946-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-ufd3bdf22b8b227ad12-1.text: improving public access to medical care, general education and secondary vocational education, and services provided by cultural and physical culture and sports organizations;
spatial-ufd3bdf22b8b227ad12-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u4efe8e0315d8168a9a-1.text: ensuring conditions for the creation of new experimental settlements implementing new approaches in demographic, housing, economic and technological policy;
spatial-u4efe8e0315d8168a9a-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u6e30715e6cce15e5eb-1.text: creating conditions to ensure the stability of the settlement system in the Russian Federation, including conditions to halt the outflow of permanent residents from regions of Siberia, the Far East and the Arctic, small and medium-sized cities and rural territories, through:
spatial-u6e30715e6cce15e5eb-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u66e33a09852e1565a5-1.text: improving staffing levels in medical, educational, cultural and physical culture and sports organizations located in rural settlements, primarily anchor settlements, and supporting the creation of employment opportunities in those territories;
spatial-u66e33a09852e1565a5-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-uad7cfffecd0dcd9840-1.text: supporting border municipalities by developing anchor settlements within their territories that ensure the national security of the Russian Federation;
spatial-uad7cfffecd0dcd9840-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u6a3419ca6652219853-1.text: preventing population outflows and maintaining the quality of life in border municipalities adjoining the Russian Federation’s state border with unfriendly states by reducing economic dependence on unfriendly states through cooperative links with enterprises in the Russian Federation and other countries;
spatial-u6a3419ca6652219853-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u0369449f889abe169e-1.text: improving amenities and the provision of utilities infrastructure, including centralized water supply and wastewater disposal, and energy supply in anchor settlements, primarily in Siberia, the Far East and the Arctic;
spatial-u0369449f889abe169e-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u63ceec4c3e5f4be443-1.text: creating territories of environmental well-being through measures to preserve and restore the natural environment and ensure the environmental quality necessary for a comfortable and safe human life and sustainable economic development;
spatial-u63ceec4c3e5f4be443-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u883f1c23096c25fc0b-1.text: assisting the resettlement of citizens living in areas exposed to hazardous natural processes, including inundation, waterlogging, avalanche, mudflow and landslide zones and others;
spatial-u883f1c23096c25fc0b-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u3238fa21ed6581e4f9-1.text: improving the safety of the population’s living environment, including creating conditions to ensure law and order, among other things by organizing the operation of local police posts in settlements in accordance with legislation and regulatory legal acts;
spatial-u3238fa21ed6581e4f9-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u33014c453461fd5c0d-1.text: creating conditions to reduce the risk of labor shortages in order to ensure economic growth in the territories of the Russian Federation through:
spatial-u33014c453461fd5c0d-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-ub4eca720ab66a3795d-1.text: expanding the geographical coverage and improving the implementation mechanism of regional labor productivity enhancement programs in constituent entities of the Russian Federation, primarily those with low labor productivity;
spatial-ub4eca720ab66a3795d-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-uc0c96d58ec1ec453b2-1.text: forecasting the economy’s personnel requirements over a 5-year period;
spatial-uc0c96d58ec1ec453b2-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u8262a7591ed66c018e-1.text: training specialists of the education system with account taken of the forecast of the economy’s personnel requirements over a 5-year period;
spatial-u8262a7591ed66c018e-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u8935bf570ceb2ab93e-1.text: improving the effectiveness of measures regulating the number of foreign workers recruited, including on the basis of the actual situation in the Russian labor market and its trends, taking account of the needs of the Russian Federation’s economy and the interests of its citizens;
spatial-u8935bf570ceb2ab93e-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u044121eeeb8b764ab4-1.text: encouraging labor mobility with account taken of territories’ personnel requirements, including through:
spatial-u044121eeeb8b764ab4-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-uedcda11cad8749b306-1.text: implementing state support measures financed from federal and regional budgets to increase labor mobility;
spatial-uedcda11cad8749b306-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-ucb763f40079a62602d-1.text: expanding the geographical coverage and improving the implementation mechanism of regional labor mobility enhancement programs in constituent entities of the Russian Federation where attracting labor resources is a priority;
spatial-ucb763f40079a62602d-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-ufb884732fcd84dd3d1-1.text: developing a modern rental housing stock in constituent entities of the Russian Federation using commercial, corporate and targeted preferential rental mechanisms;
spatial-ufb884732fcd84dd3d1-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u9bc177daf35e1f949a-1.text: ensuring transport connectivity between labor-surplus and labor-shortage territories, including the development of small-scale and medium-haul aviation to meet the labor needs of remote territories through rotational work arrangements;
spatial-u9bc177daf35e1f949a-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u6b8c3045a1e5564712-1.text: developing suburban railway infrastructure to support urban agglomeration development;
spatial-u6b8c3045a1e5564712-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-udf881065b3deb805eb-1.text: establishing and improving minimum standards for social-sector services for citizens engaged in rotational work, primarily in anchor settlements where new investment projects with a substantial impact on the territory’s economy are being implemented;
spatial-udf881065b3deb805eb-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-ubc525d9429bbe783e3-1.text: reducing interregional and intraregional disparities in the socioeconomic development of constituent entities of the Russian Federation through:
spatial-ubc525d9429bbe783e3-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-ua742ea091073dcc948-1.text: increasing the fiscal capacity of constituent entities of the Russian Federation and municipalities and their autonomy in addressing socioeconomic development tasks;
spatial-ua742ea091073dcc948-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-uf09d7fc2bb81d5ffc4-1.text: reducing wage disparities, including by introducing a new remuneration system for employees of budget-funded institutions;
spatial-uf09d7fc2bb81d5ffc4-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u884722042c6f5bc4a9-1.text: expanding and improving the effectiveness of repayable financial support instruments for infrastructure development;
spatial-u884722042c6f5bc4a9-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-ud6ee430d4f63061f8c-1.text: implementing individual socioeconomic development programs and integrated state programs for the development of geostrategic territories of the Russian Federation;
spatial-ud6ee430d4f63061f8c-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u8aee8130f9569ed74f-1.text: revising the list of single-industry municipalities of the Russian Federation (single-industry towns) on the basis of current sectoral and other trends and the risks of deterioration in their socioeconomic situation;
spatial-u8aee8130f9569ed74f-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u5bf2da484d7919e827-1.text: updating criteria for establishing special economic zones in terms of giving priority to their creation in territories less well provided with such zones, and taking account of the main development tasks of anchor settlements;
spatial-u5bf2da484d7919e827-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u7d7e753b048697dcbb-1.text: improving the competitiveness of priority development territories and special economic zones, including in comparison with similar preferential regimes and investment sites operating in foreign states;
spatial-u7d7e753b048697dcbb-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-udb829cf160ae4cea19-1.text: transitioning to a single-tier system of municipal organization in territories with low population density, while retaining, where necessary, territorial departments of the urban or municipal okrug administration and necessary social infrastructure in former centers of rural and urban settlements;
spatial-udb829cf160ae4cea19-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u65b0b131350422919e-1.text: promoting employment diversification and expanding support for residents’ entrepreneurial initiatives, including in rural areas;
spatial-u65b0b131350422919e-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u44601e41d4e8185e4e-1.text: synchronizing infrastructure development plans among constituent entities of the Russian Federation and municipalities;
spatial-u44601e41d4e8185e4e-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u302b09849bca9eb202-1.text: ensuring the development of settlements, including single-industry towns, at risk of deterioration in their socioeconomic situation, with support for them structured on a risk-based approach;
spatial-u302b09849bca9eb202-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-ud9c02a0004879abe89-1.text: ensuring efficient use of marine areas coordinated with the development of coastal territories, including through:
spatial-ud9c02a0004879abe89-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-uda0628f36cf13b6132-1.text: early identification and prevention of potential conflicts between types of marine use and a balanced approach between marine-use interests and compliance with environmental protection requirements;
spatial-uda0628f36cf13b6132-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-uaacffce40d203894a6-1.text: meeting the population’s social demands concerning the creation of highly skilled jobs, recreational needs, fishing, tourism, and the interests of indigenous and small-numbered populations;
spatial-uaacffce40d203894a6-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u5a1c34d1f3c07b9618-1.text: ensuring consistency between marine spatial planning and territorial planning at all levels of government, from federal to municipal;
spatial-u5a1c34d1f3c07b9618-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u1dcfa2a5b082890091-1.text: developing interregional (intermunicipal) and cross-border cooperation with friendly countries on the rational use of marine resources;
spatial-u1dcfa2a5b082890091-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u1e988a9fb8d8fc4204-1.text: safeguarding the interests of the Russian Federation in marine areas under its jurisdiction and in areas of the World Ocean beyond national jurisdictions.
spatial-u1e988a9fb8d8fc4204-1.locator: VII. Main Directions and Tasks of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

spatial-u157a613e5b0952b420-1.text: VIII. Spatial Development Priorities of the Russian Federation
spatial-u157a613e5b0952b420-1.locator: VIII. Spatial Development Priorities of the Russian Federation

spatial-u2b4948ba80d565ffd1-1.text: The main principles for developing transport infrastructure facilities are:

spatial-u90cec72fcd9499eabf-1.text: meeting demand for transport infrastructure by planning and prioritizing transport projects according to their socioeconomic effects on the basis of the transport and economic balance of the Russian Federation;

spatial-ud48ceb8927960d590b-1.text: ensuring transport connectivity of anchor settlements. Transport connectivity of urban agglomerations and administrative centers of constituent entities of the Russian Federation outside urban agglomerations, as well as anchor settlements that ensure the national security of the Russian Federation and serve critical infrastructure, is provided mainly by facilities of the unified core transport network, including roads forming part of it. Transport connectivity of other anchor settlements, including with settlements in adjacent territories, and of remote settlements with anchor settlements, is provided through regional and local roads, including their development and upgrading to regulatory standards, and through improved transport services for residents of those territories; where road connectivity cannot be ensured, other modes of transport are used;

spatial-u30f3761ced8e319921-1.text: improving transport accessibility and connectivity of anchor settlements and geostrategic territories of the Russian Federation through measures to reduce travel times and public transport service intervals;

spatial-u9e25310de5707d8fda-1.text: focusing on priority freight-flow directions amid the reorientation of foreign trade;

spatial-u8399b0365835fc0eec-1.text: reducing transport expenses by lowering carriage costs and optimizing routes;

spatial-ub5f9f6414e92487b5c-1.text: improving freight transport resilience by reducing transit through third countries and increasing the number of footholds for entry into friendly countries’ markets;

spatial-ubc55dd763813d26ee5-1.text: taking account of foreign states’ plans to develop alternative transit transport routes bypassing the Russian Federation in terms of their possible adverse impact on transit volumes through the country and exports of transport services.

spatial-u751f7f26c6ff44ffd1-1.text: The main transport development task is to ensure transport infrastructure development based on priority economic growth directions, economic efficiency, and improved accessibility and connectivity of territories through development of the unified core transport network and supporting infrastructure, including:

spatial-u79a620c94d8e26ba93-1.text: by improving the efficiency of existing and newly created transport infrastructure and the quality of transport services through:

spatial-ud6d874a95d8f8343c1-1.text: creating a system for decisions on transport infrastructure development based on the transport and economic balance of the Russian Federation;

spatial-u30e32911225a199bd3-1.text: implementing measures to improve state regulation of freight transport and develop long-term regulatory policy;

spatial-u6d5e86d412386e3635-1.text: introducing the take-or-pay principle, including for rail transport, primarily for low-margin freight, to prevent the creation of excess, unneeded infrastructure and support well-founded decisions when planning the use of existing transport infrastructure, including rolling stock;

spatial-ue09e1eef6afd4d1a61-1.text: constructing road bypasses around settlements, eliminating bottleneck facilities in the road and railway transport network, and reducing the share of federal roads carrying traffic under overloaded conditions;

spatial-u85d8ad5f72b5af2aa0-1.text: developing multimodal transport to improve the efficiency of the transport system as a combination of transport modes, including developing river passenger and freight transport in areas with heavily loaded rail and road networks, developing a network of hub multimodal freight transport and logistics centers and scheduled freight routes between them, promoting the freight-as-a-service model, and planning a balanced distribution of freight among transport modes;

spatial-u98a9f1ae38fb3d7ae5-1.text: containerizing freight transport and reducing delivery times for containerized cargo;

spatial-u290b9a293f87aa95d0-1.text: digitalizing freight transport procedures and document flows;

spatial-u7beb766bb2673e0524-1.text: promoting renewal of transport vehicles, including ensuring that the fleet’s average age does not exceed the prescribed standard;

spatial-u7f70e04eb07cceb923-1.text: improving road safety while reducing passenger transport travel times, including by improving the transport and operating condition of roads in the unified core transport network;

spatial-uf1550ca807d8b0f333-1.text: by ensuring year-round transport connections with remote and hard-to-reach territories, including settlements in the Arctic, Siberia and the Far East and major investment projects implemented in their adjacent territories, including by removing capacity constraints in Arctic Basin seaport infrastructure and developing transport connectivity with the administrative centers of the relevant regions, anchor settlements and border areas of friendly states;

spatial-u1df9ec1cd1602077da-1.text: by ensuring reserve throughput and carrying capacity in international transport corridors, transshipment capacity in seaports and capacity at checkpoints on the state border of the Russian Federation to eliminate infrastructure constraints on freight transport along international transport corridors and support foreign trade with the People’s Republic of China and countries of the Asia-Pacific region, the Middle East, Latin America and Africa, including through:

spatial-u2960452b7789fe2440-1.text: developing the Eastern Route International Transport Corridor, including the Eastern Railway Network, approaches to ports in the Far Eastern Basin, land checkpoints on the state border with the People’s Republic of China and Mongolia and approaches to them, and road and railway bridges in accordance with projected transport volumes;

spatial-u7458a205f68184ee09-1.text: developing trunk railway infrastructure in the central part of the Russian Federation;

spatial-u625fde16ef03d03d15-1.text: developing seaport infrastructure and the routes of the Northern Sea Route, and developing year-round navigation;

spatial-u2c7f2b8bac7fc69424-1.text: developing and renewing the fleet of large-tonnage seagoing vessels and ice-class vessels, and developing deep-water seaports;

spatial-uc5c6aa4e7f979849b6-1.text: developing the North–South International Transport Corridor, including port infrastructure in the Caspian Basin, approaches to Caspian Basin ports, land checkpoints across the state border of the Russian Federation, and direct rail container shipments along the eastern route of the North–South International Transport Corridor in accordance with projected transport volumes, and developing the Belarus–Russia–Kazakhstan–Uzbekistan–Afghanistan–Pakistan and Russia–Caspian Sea–Turkmenistan–Uzbekistan–Kyrgyzstan corridors;

spatial-u2e6d275fb26c22dac5-1.text: developing maritime routes for Russian-Indian trade along the Far East–Chennai route;

spatial-u8ef3f8a8d19aa1d5dd-1.text: coordinating and jointly implementing infrastructure development plans with neighboring friendly states interested, together with the Russian Federation, in modernizing and developing the infrastructure of transport corridors and freight routes, including the Republic of Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, the Republic of Azerbaijan and the Islamic Republic of Iran in relation to the North–South International Transport Corridor, and the People’s Republic of China and Mongolia in relation to the Eastern Route International Transport Corridor;

spatial-u25a4f3e2c6a0573e18-1.text: removing infrastructure constraints and encouraging transport on inland waterways toward the North–South International Transport Corridor, developing ports in the Azov–Black Sea Basin, the Northern Sea Route and river ports, and renewing the inland waterway fleet;

spatial-ue6c245c408529e7b28-1.text: eliminating the shortfall in carrying capacity of railway approaches to seaports in the Azov–Black Sea Basin in accordance with projected transport volumes;

spatial-u39cf23a83f4d05e427-1.text: developing additional transport corridors, including those connecting regions of the Urals, Siberian and Far Eastern Federal Districts with ports on the Arctic and Pacific Oceans, subject to confirmation of a prospective freight base;

spatial-u9a3e147119a95b572e-1.text: by developing charging and other infrastructure for transport with improved environmental performance, namely electric and hydrogen transport and transport using natural gas as motor fuel, primarily in urban agglomerations and on federal public roads forming part of the Eastern Route, Azov–Black Sea Route and North–South international transport corridors;

spatial-u8c884a534f75e8fc45-1.text: by developing an economically justified system of expressways and corresponding supporting infrastructure, including between urban agglomerations;

spatial-ub6b062057d6ac4f196-1.text: by developing an economically justified system of high-speed railway lines between urban agglomerations and providing them with rolling stock;

spatial-u91146d74901f6eb79a-1.text: by developing transport infrastructure and public transport in urban agglomerations, with priority given to infrastructure connecting remote settlements to social facilities and cultural organizations, and developing suburban passenger transport, including by creating conditions for long-term planning of suburban passenger transport in constituent entities of the Russian Federation and retaining subsidies for it;

spatial-u2ec7c94184fe988c22-1.text: by developing transport infrastructure between the Moscow urban agglomeration and constituent entities of the Central Federal District and increasing passenger transport speeds within the Central Transport Hub;

spatial-u691bbe2349e9b5012a-1.text: by developing intermunicipal and interregional roads, railways and roadside infrastructure and other infrastructure ensuring stable intermunicipal and interregional interaction and territorial connectivity, including by maintaining all facilities within the unified core transport network in conformity with regulatory standards and ensuring economically justified connectivity between settlements in adjacent territories and anchor settlements;

spatial-ud649306d4223860dcf-1.text: by increasing the population’s mobility on domestic air routes, including through:

spatial-u55bb3c122ec0d05287-1.text: establishing a network of international hub airports;

spatial-u9a95e1c95c784d3b7b-1.text: creating and developing hub airports in urban agglomerations;

spatial-u3aba63bce82e271595-1.text: reconstructing infrastructure at airports forming part of the unified core transport network;

spatial-ud0c4029bb6249de868-1.text: providing air transport for citizens at special fares from the Far East to the European part of the country and in the reverse direction;

spatial-u30ffe898292e64b34f-1.text: operating scheduled flights on socially significant routes in the Siberian and Far Eastern Federal Districts and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation.

spatial-ud603239dd34f08c713-1.text: The main principles for developing infrastructure facilities of the Russian Federation’s fuel and energy complex are:

spatial-u19de0c623ddb7f7617-1.text: affordable, guaranteed provision of fuel and energy products and services to the population and the national economy at the lowest cost;

spatial-ud625a536a4d890c1a1-1.text: improving the efficiency of use (utilization) of existing and newly created energy infrastructure in constituent entities of the Russian Federation, including through the introduction of the take-or-pay principle;

spatial-ueefc743ff8dd56fc7f-1.text: ensuring flexibility in regulating the load on electricity infrastructure to improve the efficiency of its use.

spatial-ua23095d541b5c2ebbe-1.text: The main energy development tasks are:

spatial-uc87a00c71f7c98428a-1.text: improving the quality and efficiency of energy supply to consumers, removing development constraints associated with fuel and energy infrastructure, and ensuring that electricity systems can operate in a technically independent manner:

spatial-u3c5170a2ad7830f1fa-1.text: by ensuring medium- and long-term forecasts of energy consumption that take account of spatial development tasks, forecast economic needs, including those of settlements where new investment projects with a substantial impact on the territory’s economy are being implemented, the potential for improving energy efficiency, economically justified reductions in greenhouse gas emissions, and climate change and its associated risks and opportunities;

spatial-uaba57528528c2d7010-1.text: by ensuring the prescribed level of supply-demand adequacy in reliability zones within interconnected power systems, including by reducing wear and tear on energy infrastructure facilities through determination of the generation-capacity mix on the basis of socioeconomic, technical and technological, environmental and climatic criteria, primarily in Eastern Siberia, the Far East, the Southern and North Caucasian Federal Districts, anchor settlements and border territories;

spatial-u3a76abbaa58a1ca96a-1.text: by ensuring flexibility in regulating connection to and disconnection from electricity grids when surplus capacity is used, including for digital-currency mining;

spatial-ucaf82f8369982d8b7f-1.text: by removing infrastructure constraints, including developing grid infrastructure and generation facilities for the Moscow urban agglomeration, the Southern and North Caucasian Federal Districts, Eastern Siberia, the Far East and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation, to prevent potential electricity shortages;

spatial-ud36a8fac8a76f3c620-1.text: by encouraging advance development and deployment of energy-saving and energy-efficient technologies, primarily in the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation, the Far North and areas equated to it;

spatial-ua9a8cf652d7909cdde-1.text: by ensuring optimal development of energy infrastructure in remote and hard-to-reach territories with the necessary natural conditions and resources, for their economic development and to prevent population outflows;

spatial-ue391bfd63f634348c9-1.text: developing infrastructure for electricity exports and interterritorial supplies, primarily to regions with growing electricity demand;

spatial-u6c84b5e6575cf718b7-1.text: developing modern energy infrastructure using energy storage systems and renewable energy sources, including in remote and isolated territories;

spatial-u36f2dfd379ca35aa48-1.text: improving the quality and efficiency of the system supplying gas to consumers:

spatial-u7171b36aa5686cbf13-1.text: by extending gas connections, including to social-sector facilities such as medical organizations, and ensuring economically efficient gasification of anchor settlements, primarily in Eastern Siberia, the Far East and the Arctic, where a substantial share of households remain without gas; in 2023, gasification coverage of the population was 29.8 percent in the Siberian Federal District and 25.2 percent in the Far Eastern Federal District, compared with the Russian Federation average of 73.8 percent;

spatial-uf101f23d269fdb6835-1.text: by meeting growing gas demand from industrial consumers and transport in an economically efficient manner;

spatial-u0c2d0a3cdff27c8d60-1.text: by ensuring expansion, modernization and optimization of the capacity of the unified gas supply system, taking account of the need for new export routes, and by creating gas transport infrastructure in Eastern Siberia, the Far East and the Arctic with the possibility of integrating it into the unified gas supply system;

spatial-ufe51af04201430f912-1.text: by developing infrastructure for domestic use and export of liquefied natural gas, including through ports in the Arctic Ocean;

spatial-u045add09e283569ac0-1.text: by developing infrastructure to expand the use of natural gas as motor fuel;

spatial-uf8be5b3c9505f4e7ff-1.text: ensuring expansion and modernization of the trunk oil and petroleum-product pipeline system to diversify export flows of Russian oil and petroleum products, including expansion of pipeline infrastructure capabilities at the ports of Primorsk, Novorossiysk and Kozmino, and to develop oil refining and petrochemical production in the Russian Federation.

spatial-u3035d84a40a0661d45-1.text: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services
spatial-u3035d84a40a0661d45-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-u9019d8d84fc836d011-1.text: The main principles for developing housing construction and housing and utilities services are:
spatial-u9019d8d84fc836d011-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-ua137b5172db8ed57b1-1.text: ensuring a differentiated approach to state support measures for housing construction in different territories, including with account taken of housing provision and demand, while giving priority to urban agglomerations and anchor settlements where major investment projects substantially affecting the economy and employment growth are being implemented, and to geostrategic territories of the Russian Federation;
spatial-ua137b5172db8ed57b1-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-u902a986b0a8fd2c0c1-1.text: encouraging medium- and low-rise housing development and individual housing development in territories adjacent to urban agglomeration cores and in small and medium-sized cities and rural settlements;
spatial-u902a986b0a8fd2c0c1-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-uf9ba7d501dcc27df7e-1.text: encouraging increased construction of spacious dwellings for families with children;
spatial-uf9ba7d501dcc27df7e-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-u193e217e5ffe404568-1.text: applying an integrated approach to ensuring the quality of the urban environment:
spatial-u193e217e5ffe404568-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-ub40328c41e244fc6af-1.text: maintaining a balance between housing development and infrastructure provision, encouraging multifunctional urban areas and improving the efficiency of use of existing built-up areas;
spatial-ub40328c41e244fc6af-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-uda5c367ee64f2ee4d6-1.text: improving the implementation effectiveness of apartment-building capital repair programs, prioritizing work affecting service life, improving the financial sustainability of capital repair programs, and prioritizing measures and work aimed at energy saving and greater energy efficiency in the existing housing stock when carrying out capital repairs;
spatial-uda5c367ee64f2ee4d6-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-ub2ec29986c5c0d298f-1.text: ensuring a balanced tariff regulation model in housing and utilities services;
spatial-ub2ec29986c5c0d298f-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-u704ab5c1b03bf06017-1.text: reducing territorial disparities in the provision of housing and utilities infrastructure;
spatial-u704ab5c1b03bf06017-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-ue17364147a3638ecd2-1.text: ensuring economic efficiency in housing and utilities services through new technologies, lean construction and digitalization;
spatial-ue17364147a3638ecd2-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-ue0a64cd2708762eb38-1.text: using public-private partnership mechanisms in housing and utilities projects.
spatial-ue0a64cd2708762eb38-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-u3af6020c6f694d3048-1.text: The main tasks for developing housing construction and housing and utilities services are:
spatial-u3af6020c6f694d3048-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-u36d643db2ec38b8dc2-1.text: creating conditions for medium- and low-rise housing construction and individual housing construction in territories adjacent to urban agglomeration cores, in small and medium-sized cities and in rural areas, excluding zones potentially exposed to hazardous natural processes, including:
spatial-u36d643db2ec38b8dc2-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-u3bebec40fce7c50bf7-1.text: by improving the quality of the living environment through the creation of necessary utilities, transport and social infrastructure in anchor settlements and the development of individual and low-rise housing construction in anchor settlements and adjacent territories where major investment projects substantially affecting the economy and employment growth are being implemented, and in territories adjacent to urban agglomeration cores;
spatial-u3bebec40fce7c50bf7-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-u986143cca7498c1d3e-1.text: by creating accessible mechanisms for financing individual residential construction, including mechanisms enabling individual housing construction facilities to connect (technologically connect) to utility networks at an affordable price;
spatial-u986143cca7498c1d3e-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-u2dba84b260cf577ed9-1.text: by creating conditions for modular construction, the production and use of prefabricated home kits, and accelerated release into use of land plots intended for individual and low-rise housing construction;
spatial-u2dba84b260cf577ed9-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-u4db37cff73eb314c4c-1.text: improving legislation governing state support measures for integrated territorial development projects;
spatial-u4db37cff73eb314c4c-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-ub3fdba4d234f1dc72f-1.text: developing mechanisms, including nonprofit rental arrangements, to provide housing for the population, including to attract new personnel, in settlements where major investment projects with a substantial impact on the territory’s economy are being implemented, and in settlements located in geostrategic territories of the Russian Federation;
spatial-ub3fdba4d234f1dc72f-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-u0222d30c843e5c0e07-1.text: improving mechanisms for relocating residents from unsafe housing and declaring housing unsafe, including amendments to legislation on unsafe housing aimed at reducing the burden on the budget system;
spatial-u0222d30c843e5c0e07-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-ue7ec618322e84c8bec-1.text: improving the effectiveness of tariff-based sources for financing capital expenditure in housing and utilities services;
spatial-ue7ec618322e84c8bec-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-u6ce0b2ca8411b2c4f6-1.text: increasing the attractiveness of housing and utilities services to private-company investment.
spatial-u6ce0b2ca8411b2c4f6-1.locator: Housing Construction and Housing and Utilities Services

spatial-u72e1236b8648b15801-1.text: Planning the development of social infrastructure is based on the following principles:

spatial-u34f0b586fb71e4c185-1.text: provision of infrastructure in anchor settlements in accordance with standards, including to ensure access to education, medical care, social care and cultural services and meet other needs of residents of adjacent territories;

spatial-ud58a79edc93fc281e0-1.text: taking account of existing infrastructure, including private infrastructure, and the population’s needs in light of population density and transport accessibility of social infrastructure facilities, including the establishment of centers providing services, medical care, education and social care to several constituent entities of the Russian Federation or municipalities;

spatial-u0b4ad3294348900d8a-1.text: taking account of planned capacity utilization when creating new infrastructure facilities, primarily expensive and highly specialized ones, to maximize the efficiency of their use and prevent excessive budget expenditure;

spatial-ue652d0849fc04679f9-1.text: taking account, when deciding to create or expand an infrastructure facility, of the population’s age and sex composition, migration flows, attractiveness as a place to live for families with children and young people, the demographic forecast for the territory, and personnel requirements of investment projects implemented or planned in the territory; that demographic forecast and those personnel requirements must be reflected in the territory’s strategic planning documents.

spatial-ubce517df35f09e76df-1.text: A specific feature of planning sports infrastructure development is prioritizing facilities for mass-participation sport aimed at increasing the share of citizens regularly engaging in physical culture and sport.

spatial-u2d104100a49fcadead-1.text: Specific features of planning medical infrastructure development include taking account of territorial planning schemes containing maps of health facility locations that ensure access to medical organizations and patient routing in accordance with medical care procedures, and creating or developing transport infrastructure, including public transport routes, to health facilities.

spatial-ub26311278e08c16ddb-1.text: Medical infrastructure is created as a priority in anchor settlements in accordance with the general principles of social infrastructure development, while retaining opportunities to develop it in adjacent territories where a need exists, provided that the need for that infrastructure in anchor settlements has been met. Priority is given to creating medical infrastructure in anchor settlements with populations of up to 100 thousand on the basis of central district hospitals and district hospitals, including primary vascular departments, oncology care centers, admission departments, women’s consultation clinics, regional and interdistrict (district) centers providing medical care to patients with carbohydrate metabolism disorders and diabetes mellitus, and units providing medical rehabilitation care.

spatial-ua2435a1769a06e54f7-1.text: Preschool and general education infrastructure is created as a priority in anchor settlements in accordance with the general principles of social infrastructure development, while retaining opportunities to develop it in adjacent territories where a need exists, provided that the need for that infrastructure in anchor settlements has been met.

spatial-ua478a689dc0ee74fa5-1.text: Planning the development of higher and secondary vocational education infrastructure has the following specific features:

spatial-u616efde1f2be5f8520-1.text: fulfilling the priority task of training personnel needed to support implementation of the priority development directions of the federal districts of the Russian Federation and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation and the corresponding priority development directions of the relevant constituent entities of the Russian Federation, including by updating existing educational programs and developing new ones;

spatial-u837d554f89ecd703d7-1.text: in anchor settlements with populations exceeding 300 thousand, modern university campuses and higher education institutions oriented toward international scientific and educational cooperation, including exports of educational services and the education of foreign students, may be created, as may educational institutions providing secondary vocational education programs;

spatial-u3b26a891b1f85cf392-1.text: in anchor settlements with populations from 250 thousand to 500 thousand, modern university campuses, higher education institutions and educational institutions providing secondary vocational education programs may be created, primarily oriented toward training personnel for the needs of the relevant sectors and the Russian Federation’s economy as a whole;

spatial-u91f443b34755471d15-1.text: in anchor settlements with populations from 100 thousand to 250 thousand, higher education institutions and educational institutions providing secondary vocational education programs may be created, primarily oriented toward training personnel for the economic needs of the relevant constituent entity of the Russian Federation;

spatial-u5220b8ab96dd0980e0-1.text: in anchor settlements with populations of up to 100 thousand, the personnel needs of the settlement’s economy are met by creating branches of higher education institutions and developing the secondary vocational education system.

spatial-u5b1cd034fcb70e44bc-1.text: The main task in developing the social sphere is to reduce disparities in territories’ socioeconomic development by improving infrastructure provision in anchor settlements, primarily settlements ensuring the national security of the Russian Federation and serving critical infrastructure, science cities, small and medium-sized cities and rural settlements, including:

spatial-uba3e5d2be23f36d0ee-1.text: by ensuring a differentiated approach to the directions and measures of state support for developing anchor settlements and geostrategic territories of the Russian Federation, taking account of the demographic situation, characteristics of the settlement system, the level and dynamics of economic development, specific natural conditions and the role of those territories in achieving spatial development priorities;

spatial-u72a83f6a675857e86a-1.text: by developing social infrastructure based in anchor settlements, including for residents of adjacent territories, and by enabling the population to use outreach (mobile) forms of service provision;

spatial-u75bd4728f7e9db129b-1.text: by improving the competitiveness of higher education institutions, primarily in geostrategic territories of the Russian Federation;

spatial-u31b0b3ec434bcf818b-1.text: by developing information technologies that enable social services to be provided remotely.

spatial-uf26b3b095dccf3bcf4-1.text: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications
spatial-uf26b3b095dccf3bcf4-1.locator: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications

spatial-u489f83bff618d5742f-1.text: Planning the development of information and telecommunications infrastructure and the communications sector is based on the following principles:
spatial-u489f83bff618d5742f-1.locator: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications

spatial-u118b7f4cf09c7d3844-1.text: focusing on eliminating the digital divide among constituent entities of the Russian Federation through priority development of information and telecommunications infrastructure providing high-speed data transmission accessible to the population of the Russian Federation;
spatial-u118b7f4cf09c7d3844-1.locator: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications

spatial-u39625a8595e37090e1-1.text: ensuring advance development of information and telecommunications infrastructure and removing infrastructure constraints to accelerate digital technology development;
spatial-u39625a8595e37090e1-1.locator: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications

spatial-uff180376a7ed66510c-1.text: creating competitive information and telecommunications infrastructure based on domestic developments;
spatial-uff180376a7ed66510c-1.locator: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications

spatial-u2b325a341ebf228fda-1.text: synchronizing telecommunications infrastructure development with sectoral development tasks and needs;
spatial-u2b325a341ebf228fda-1.locator: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications

spatial-u6eebea957c70de0ba9-1.text: providing access to the Internet information and telecommunications network for the greatest possible number of households and institutions, including by creating access points in rural settlements;
spatial-u6eebea957c70de0ba9-1.locator: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications

spatial-u57e0b055f62a09077f-1.text: creating conditions for deploying communications networks in territories that are not economically attractive to mobile radiotelephone operators;
spatial-u57e0b055f62a09077f-1.locator: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications

spatial-ue7d734d0cbf277b78d-1.text: maintaining and improving the connectivity of the Russian Federation’s territory through traditional and modern electronic postal services.
spatial-ue7d734d0cbf277b78d-1.locator: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications

spatial-u41961a5e077d444153-1.text: The task in developing information and telecommunications infrastructure and the communications sector is to improve information and telecommunications connectivity among territories of the Russian Federation through:
spatial-u41961a5e077d444153-1.locator: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications

spatial-ud6a2516ec592a057c4-1.text: widespread use of satellite communications systems in remote and hard-to-reach territories and ensuring access to communications services, including high-speed data transmission services, for residents of those territories;
spatial-ud6a2516ec592a057c4-1.locator: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications

spatial-u4d00beaab921fd3566-1.text: continued implementation of programs to narrow the digital divide and provide modern communications services and broadband access to the Internet information and telecommunications network for rural settlements and socially significant facilities;
spatial-u4d00beaab921fd3566-1.locator: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications

spatial-uc45600464b820dd12d-1.text: accelerated development of communications infrastructure in the new constituent entities of the Russian Federation to give residents access to modern digital services at a level no lower than the national level;
spatial-uc45600464b820dd12d-1.locator: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications

spatial-uc3230f7f06237ab624-1.text: developing trunk communications lines to connect remote territories to the unified telecommunications network of the Russian Federation and provide mobile radiotelephone coverage along federal roads and trunk railways, and to increase line capacity and accommodate steadily growing traffic volumes;
spatial-uc3230f7f06237ab624-1.locator: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications

spatial-u7963e24e8005f88529-1.text: creating a hybrid communications network covering the entire country, including the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation and the Northern Sea Route;
spatial-u7963e24e8005f88529-1.locator: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications

spatial-u4115a89bac8f4e06ff-1.text: modernizing and digitally transforming postal services to enable residents and organizations throughout the Russian Federation to obtain high-quality channels for exchanging information, goods and services.
spatial-u4115a89bac8f4e06ff-1.locator: Information and Telecommunications Infrastructure and Communications

spatial-udd36fe41fe0dd7b818-1.text: The main principles of spatial development in industry are:

spatial-u7a60b73c4c05774e59-1.text: promoting the creation and development of transport, energy and other infrastructure for mineral resource centers containing large and unique deposits of strategic mineral resources, including hydrocarbons and/or scarce types of solid minerals, and planning facilities associated with hydrocarbon extraction and mining and beneficiation complexes;

spatial-u95abded8e2e81023e0-1.text: promoting the location of manufacturing facilities in territories with sufficient transport, energy and other infrastructure;

spatial-u70c17bb85332f53315-1.text: planning industrial infrastructure development to improve the territorial organization of the economy, proceeding from the need to:

spatial-u694389c7db3f9dc984-1.text: encourage the creation of industrial parks and industrial technology parks, taking account of the priority development of geostrategic territories of the Russian Federation and territories with high potential for deeper processing of raw materials, particularly the Siberian Federal District, and implementation of the priority development directions of the federal districts of the Russian Federation and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation;

spatial-u3630c1dfb0cefb7a20-1.text: provide industrial projects with regional industrial infrastructure and social infrastructure to attract labor resources, taking account of the priority of projects included in national technological leadership projects, technological sovereignty projects, including in the radioelectronics industry, and projects producing critical industrial products, meaning products included in sectoral import substitution plans;

spatial-u92d7eb494ede4cdb37-1.text: prioritize construction and reconstruction of regional industrial infrastructure facilities within industrial parks and industrial technology parks and according to the development needs of industrial clusters;

spatial-ud35cc97a11c3daab40-1.text: encourage the location of manufacturing facilities, including construction-material production, close to the sites of investment projects requiring their products, in order to minimize delivery distances.

spatial-uf666cf9d14622cae41-1.text: Environment, Natural Resource Management and Climate Change Adaptation

spatial-u263b1934e746323d1f-1.text: The main principles of spatial development in environmental protection and natural resource management, including development of the mineral resource base, and in climate change adaptation are:

spatial-ua1f392fbc24eea8fc5-1.text: ensuring rational and efficient use and renewal of natural resources;

spatial-u3facfdb8211eb3c9d3-1.text: reducing vulnerability to adverse impacts caused by climate change and using the potential arising from its positive effects;

spatial-uab0bd2ff9e572937e7-1.text: concentrating the efforts and resources of the state and organizations on geological exploration of the subsurface and subsurface use, predominantly within mineral resource centers being developed;

spatial-u31b0d4e9daf160ce5a-1.text: supporting adoption of best available technologies and expansion of goods production and service provision using secondary raw materials by economic entities in all sectors of the economy.

spatial-u5ef3549a784f0e9eee-1.text: The main spatial development tasks in environmental protection and natural resource management are:

spatial-u772d7d5b630e503fa0-1.text: developing the mineral resource base, including by increasing geological study of the subsurface and mineral exploration, primarily in the Far Eastern and Siberian Federal Districts and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation;

spatial-uf85c2a93ee2a55132f-1.text: reducing total emissions of hazardous pollutants into the ambient air in cities participating in the Clean Air federal project, primarily in the Far Eastern and Siberian Federal Districts;

spatial-u4be07b45a72011673e-1.text: reducing discharges of polluted wastewater and restoring the ecological health of major water bodies, primarily the Volga, Don, Amur and Ural Rivers;

spatial-u2e2ad9b1ec0b3d8c7b-1.text: protecting the population and economic facilities against adverse effects of water, primarily in flood-prone territories;

spatial-u0616d13ca3b2598fa8-1.text: meeting drinking and domestic water supply needs and agricultural water needs in water-deficient territories;

spatial-ud4128b9fd695c472dc-1.text: introducing circular economy principles and resource-saving approaches at the regional level, proceeding from the need to minimize the generation of production and consumption waste;

spatial-u874f39e8719fd1505c-1.text: creating infrastructure for managing production and consumption waste and secondary raw materials, including eco-industrial parks;

spatial-u2a887187688878c5c8-1.text: eliminating sites of accumulated environmental damage that threaten the population and the environment, primarily those located on industrial sites in Usolye-Sibirskoye in Irkutsk Oblast, at the former Baikal Pulp and Paper Mill Open Joint Stock Company, and at the Krasny Bor industrial waste landfill;

spatial-u9568e15e728c01fb7b-1.text: preserving the unique ecosystem of the Baikal Natural Territory;

spatial-ub42a8a14d13c9631ca-1.text: creating ecotourism infrastructure in national parks, taking account of maximum permissible recreational capacity and their special protection regime and on the basis of park recreation planning;

spatial-u9c1e69002cc4e60791-1.text: ensuring a balance between forest conservation and loss and the socioeconomic development of settlements and economic facilities;

spatial-ubb515e32a64e710868-1.text: implementing measures in constituent entities of the Russian Federation to restore agroforestry land-improvement systems, increase soil fertility and crop yields, and prevent desertification.

spatial-u13d5f6cee4d2c9ea5f-1.text: The main spatial development task in climate change adaptation is to develop and implement measures protecting property and the vital interests of individuals, society and the state against hazardous natural phenomena and climate change, including through:

spatial-uad3bc193b7dc61a623-1.text: implementing climate change adaptation measures at federal, sectoral, regional and corporate levels;

spatial-u5caceafd7fab9601c4-1.text: improving early warning systems for natural disasters and extreme, anomalous and hazardous hydrometeorological processes and phenomena, including developing the state observation network and infrastructure for monitoring and forecasting hazardous hydrometeorological phenomena, including wider and more effective use of remote methods and artificial intelligence;

spatial-u4322222f078f689c68-1.text: maintaining federal, sectoral and regional lists of climate-vulnerable facilities;

spatial-u5dba1d8bf64ceca28f-1.text: using regional climate change adaptation plans when updating strategic planning documents developed at constituent-entity and municipal levels and determining the need for engineering facilities protecting territories against hazardous natural processes and phenomena;

spatial-uf77e8f851b691482a8-1.text: taking account of transboundary risks and effects when making climate change adaptation decisions and preparing coordinated adaptation measures of a transboundary nature;

spatial-u814e3fdce137f0527d-1.text: taking account of the prevalence and level of climate risks and the climate change adaptation measures being implemented when preparing territorial planning documents, urban zoning documents and territorial layout documentation for cities and urban settlements.

spatial-uc912a731f21a892414-1.text: The main spatial development principles for the tourism industry, an important component of the supply-side economy, are:

spatial-u1441061b41a68afe2a-1.text: providing sufficient tourism infrastructure to meet growing demand for domestic and inbound tourism;

spatial-u3032a9c43ee5c87fb2-1.text: realizing territories’ natural, cultural, historical, health-improvement and other recreational potential, including to reduce disparities in territories’ socioeconomic development through tourists transferring resources from places of earning to places of leisure;

spatial-ue3fe2483b8ecdb40a3-1.text: ensuring transport accessibility of tourism facilities.

spatial-u81ce7614cc4bf269ba-1.text: The main spatial development tasks in tourism are:

spatial-ud986606cd00d504fa9-1.text: developing tourism infrastructure by increasing accommodation capacity and the number and capacity of resorts, amusement parks and other tourist attractions, primarily through private capital, including through:

spatial-uaf0d36ace306ec69f4-1.text: aligning programs at all levels, including in culture, environmental protection, rural development and the creation of a comfortable urban environment, with the tasks of increasing the number of tourist trips within the Russian Federation;

spatial-u355a905366b48d0293-1.text: removing excessive restrictions on land use and other regulatory restrictions hindering tourism infrastructure development;

spatial-u5089b86323e800014b-1.text: creating new resorts in territories with potential to attract tourists, including implementing the Five Seas and Lake Baikal project;

spatial-u5a96bbb4aa15467307-1.text: prioritizing projects to create the transport, utilities and energy infrastructure needed to support tourism facilities.

spatial-u197496c690e8dab25a-1.text: The main principles of spatial development in scientific and technological development are:

spatial-u9bb77e08ebd4dfc4e7-1.text: intensifying interregional cooperation in innovation when implementing projects aimed at finding high-technology solutions;

spatial-u5d7295062e97dbb7af-1.text: encouraging research and developing the infrastructure of entities engaged in scientific, scientific and technical, and innovative activities, enabling significant scientific and technical results and the creation and deployment of domestic knowledge-intensive technologies;

spatial-u981e7960dbf254bd97-1.text: concentrating intellectual, financial, organizational and infrastructure resources on supporting scientific and scientific-technical programs and projects covering the full innovation cycle, needed to respond to regional, nationwide and international challenges;

spatial-u6f68fa8c3a15cc4199-1.text: state and public support for fundamental and exploratory scientific research as an instrument for the country’s long-term development in regions with the relevant existing capabilities.

spatial-u1e12586e4a0687d527-1.text: The main spatial development tasks in scientific and technological development are:

spatial-u9c2fd5555beecf357f-1.text: creating conditions and incentives for cooperation between regions with a weak scientific and technological base and major scientific and educational centers, and developing technology transfer on that basis;

spatial-u86b00459d1d9af81f4-1.text: supporting scientific and technological development in science cities outside million-plus cities and regional administrative centers, and expanding the geographical coverage of support for scientific and technological activities;

spatial-ucf591419bb2ae7f869-1.text: ensuring links and interaction between scientific organizations and higher education institutions, including by ensuring their geographical proximity;

spatial-u778ac318be63d3b5af-1.text: stimulating demand for high-technology products from state authorities and budget-funded institutions of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, regional development institutions, large private companies and public companies with state participation;

spatial-uf3296c3233cc7d4e46-1.text: increasing domestic expenditure on research and development, including through greater private business investment for these purposes;

spatial-u68159e50a53746f478-1.text: stimulating the supply of high-technology products in the regions by ensuring favorable conditions for the emergence of new high-technology companies and the development of existing ones;

spatial-u31537405677d37ccc2-1.text: creating infrastructure and conditions for research and development and the deployment of knowledge-intensive technologies that meet modern principles for organizing scientific, scientific and technical, and innovative activities, based on the best Russian and international practices;

spatial-u801f113929927364d9-1.text: implementing measures to overcome socioeconomic development constraints and stimulate research projects in science cities;

spatial-ud3ad448bee505d4edc-1.text: supporting existing local scientific and technological capabilities in coordination with the region’s industrial development, including support for local higher education institutions and scientific organizations with growth potential;

spatial-uab251a425e8b970d52-1.text: supporting regional scientific groups in advancing from regional to federal and international levels;

spatial-u0ea8508b4d541cce72-1.text: creating opportunities to identify and retain in the region talented young people capable of pursuing careers in science and technology;

spatial-u6db80dd290f7a5e4a5-1.text: creating a regional support system for small technology companies that ensures their accelerated growth and stable position in national and global markets;

spatial-ue3ae69f44ff1abc4ef-1.text: establishing a qualified regional commissioning entity based on partnership among the region, the state, industry, science and higher education, pooling public and private resources for research, experimental design and technological work, clearly allocating functions, powers and responsibilities, and accelerating the introduction of Russian knowledge-intensive technologies and products into the economy;

spatial-uec3b85e88479f38a89-1.text: locating major international scientific projects in promising constituent entities of the Russian Federation to address tasks associated with responding to grand challenges, primarily in urban agglomerations and science cities;

spatial-uaf5e346123e5f1cc7b-1.text: shifting from simultaneous efforts across a broad range of regional scientific and technological development challenges to prioritizing limited resources on selected challenges;

spatial-ubba0577725c9396327-1.text: strengthening the role of the region’s key higher education institutions and scientific organizations as drivers of technological development;

spatial-uf5ca8329e2537393db-1.text: creating and developing a network of regional development institutions that support and finance technology companies’ production projects through project financing;

spatial-u435d5a1d0462006586-1.text: creating mechanisms to encourage investors to develop infrastructure in territories with preferential regimes where critical and cross-cutting technologies are created;

spatial-ub4ff4099f748083a2a-1.text: developing an interregional network of technology transfer centers operating under a unified standard and interaction procedures.

spatial-ue5b5b0b8fc0f5fe8fc-1.text: IX. Priority Development Directions for Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation within the Federal Districts of the Russian Federation and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation, and for New Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation
spatial-ue5b5b0b8fc0f5fe8fc-1.locator: IX. Priority Development Directions for Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation within the Federal Districts of the Russian Federation and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation, and for New Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation

spatial-u3c5fe5b39b716a7784-1.text: To determine priorities for state support and concentrate resources, the main development directions of the federal districts of the Russian Federation, the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation and the new constituent entities of the Russian Federation have been established; in the Strategy, these are understood as prospective economic specializations of constituent entities of the Russian Federation.
spatial-u3c5fe5b39b716a7784-1.locator: IX. Priority Development Directions for Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation within the Federal Districts of the Russian Federation and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation, and for New Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation

spatial-u6d2426974d03251c0b-1.text: Taking account of those directions, the executive bodies of constituent entities of the Russian Federation determine the priority socioeconomic development directions of the respective constituent entities of the Russian Federation.
spatial-u6d2426974d03251c0b-1.locator: IX. Priority Development Directions for Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation within the Federal Districts of the Russian Federation and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation, and for New Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation

spatial-u6f50f2842c1b6943b1-1.text: In the Strategy, the federal districts of the Russian Federation, the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation and the new constituent entities of the Russian Federation are understood as macroregions of the Russian Federation.
spatial-u6f50f2842c1b6943b1-1.locator: IX. Priority Development Directions for Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation within the Federal Districts of the Russian Federation and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation, and for New Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation

spatial-u6762e7dc77393a4b7b-1.text: The Far Eastern Federal District and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation
spatial-u6762e7dc77393a4b7b-1.locator: The Far Eastern Federal District and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation

spatial-ua0377edf96d1fe92f7-1.text: The main development directions for the Far Eastern Federal District and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation include:
spatial-ua0377edf96d1fe92f7-1.locator: The Far Eastern Federal District and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation

spatial-u92ee0f54486803a177-1.text: renewal of Far Eastern anchor settlements and development of Arctic anchor settlements, including through measures provided for in long-term development plans for those settlements, including measures to develop the Vladivostok urban agglomeration and Vladivostok’s satellite city;
spatial-u92ee0f54486803a177-1.locator: The Far Eastern Federal District and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation

spatial-ucdf4c57238d5a76abe-1.text: developing transport infrastructure, including the Baikal–Amur Mainline, the Trans-Siberian Railway, the Northern Sea Route and export-supporting infrastructure, namely seaports in the Eastern Basin, checkpoints across the state border of the Russian Federation and approaches to them, and roads linking seaports with transport and logistics centers; and developing air services and airfield infrastructure;
spatial-ucdf4c57238d5a76abe-1.locator: The Far Eastern Federal District and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation

spatial-u51eec6bc74dc62b7ea-1.text: meeting the economy’s current and prospective needs for electricity and capacity, including by building new generating facilities, modernizing existing generation and constructing power grid facilities specified in electricity development planning documents, and on the basis of the results of market mechanisms;
spatial-u51eec6bc74dc62b7ea-1.locator: The Far Eastern Federal District and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation

spatial-u6b31720c636299b0ff-1.text: increasing output in export-oriented, knowledge-intensive and high-technology sectors, synchronized with the development of science and education and ensuring the competitiveness of the Far Eastern Federal District within the Russian Federation and the Asia-Pacific region;
spatial-u6b31720c636299b0ff-1.locator: The Far Eastern Federal District and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation

spatial-ua5e02463764616e9ec-1.text: developing tourism and tourism infrastructure, including by improving the connectivity of the Far Eastern Federal District with other territories of the Russian Federation and Asia-Pacific countries and connectivity among constituent entities of the Russian Federation within the Far Eastern Federal District, through the expansion of visa-free agreements with neighboring states;
spatial-ua5e02463764616e9ec-1.locator: The Far Eastern Federal District and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation

spatial-u667ec956e0e37d06cb-1.text: implementing investment projects aimed at industrial cooperation with friendly Asia-Pacific countries, including in international priority development territories in border areas of Primorsky, Khabarovsk and Zabaykalsky Krais, Amur Oblast and the Jewish Autonomous Oblast.
spatial-u667ec956e0e37d06cb-1.locator: The Far Eastern Federal District and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation

spatial-uc9a742a842cefcef31-1.text: The main development directions for the Volga Federal District include:

spatial-ub2601f0a369e526bf8-1.text: developing agricultural and food-processing machinery manufacturing, automotive manufacturing, aircraft manufacturing and shipbuilding, as well as the chemical industry and petroleum-product production, including through industrial clusters;

spatial-u88055e893ed0609475-1.text: developing agriculture, including agricultural processing, among other things through highly efficient technologies and higher labor productivity;

spatial-u8885dd8541b80d810a-1.text: using the infrastructure of the Volga–Kama Basin to realize the logistics and transit potential of the Volga Federal District, including creating modern terminals and ensuring guaranteed depths along the main routes in order to shift some freight bound for ports in the Azov–Black Sea and Caspian Basins to inland water transport;

spatial-ub349253d90e98eec69-1.text: developing interregional tourist routes, including the Great Volga Route national tourist route;

spatial-uaa67598e7e5920bad0-1.text: developing the scientific and innovative potential of the Volga Federal District, including taking account of enterprises’ need for qualified personnel.

spatial-ub6d9f113fba5e94f40-1.text: The main development directions for the Northwestern Federal District include:

spatial-ud82fd744022b54ae32-1.text: implementing projects in artificial intelligence and high technologies, primarily in mineral extraction, pharmaceuticals, genetic technologies and energy security;

spatial-u714ad34bea9e9d0d08-1.text: creating an interregional automotive industry cluster, including on the sites of former automotive production facilities in Saint Petersburg and Kaliningrad and Leningrad Oblasts;

spatial-u84e5ff2c6c766c0c5a-1.text: removing infrastructure constraints on balanced use of port capacity, including by eliminating bottlenecks on railway approaches to Baltic and Arctic Basin seaports, on the transport security of Kaliningrad Oblast, and on gasification of certain constituent entities of the Russian Federation, primarily Murmansk Oblast and the Republic of Karelia;
